- [passage] 2. Before creating the index, validate that no documents in the collection violate the index constraints. If a collection is distributed across shards and a shard contains a chunk with duplicate documents, the create index operation may succeed on the shards without duplicates but not on the shard with duplicates. To avoid leaving inconsistent indexes across shards, you can issue the [`db.collection.dropIndex()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropindex.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.dropIndex) from a [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) to drop the index from the collection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/build-indexes-on-sharded-clusters.md#before-you-begin · keywords: index, sharded query targeting, db.collection.dropIndex(), mongos · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md

- [passage] | Aspect | Atlas Core | Atlas Infinite | | --- | --- | --- | | Architecture | Compute and storage run on the same node. Each data-bearing node runs on a virtual machine with attached storage. | Compute and storage run as independent layers. MongoDB manages the storage layer separately from the compute nodes. | | Compute scaling | You change compute capacity by selecting a different cluster tier. Atlas restarts the cluster's nodes when you change the tier, with no downtime on dedicated clusters. | You scale the cluster tier independently of storage. Scaling doesn't move your data, so it is fast. | | Storage scaling | You scale storage capacity and IOPS independently of compute on dedicated clusters, up to the maximum for the cluster tier. To add capacity beyond that maximum, you scale to a higher tier. | Storage capacity increases automatically based on usage, independently of the cluster tier, without downtime. | | Horizontal scaling | You shard a cluster when its data approaches the storage capacity, and add workload-specific nodes, like read-only or analytics nodes, as needed. | Higher storage capacity means you can store up to 128TB on a single shard without sharding. Adding workload-specific nodes is much faster. | | Recovery | Atlas monitors your database regularly, and performs auto-healing if it discovers an issue. If it replaces a node, the new node performs an initial sync before it serves queries. | Atlas monitors your database regularly, and performs auto-healing if it discovers an issue. If it replaces a node, the new node immediately connects to the storage layer, with no need for an initial sync. | | Cloud provider and tier availability | Free clusters, Flex clusters, and dedicated cluster tiers, on AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. | Public preview: `M10` through `M60` replica sets in supported AWS regions, with storage capacity up to 128 TB per replica set. | | Feature coverage | Supports the full Atlas feature set. | Some Atlas features aren't [supported during public preview.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/infinite/atlas-infinite-landing.md#std-label-atlas-infinite-availability) | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/index.md#compare-editions · keywords: sharded query targeting, M10, M60

This allows for targeted operations as a mongos can route the operations to only the shards that contain the required data. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/sharding/ · keywords: sharded query targeting

## How it works

- [passage] When a shard receives a query, it uses the most efficient index available to fulfill that query. The index used may be either the [shard key index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharding-shard-key-indexes.md#std-label-sharding-shard-key-indexes) or another eligible index present on the shard. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md#index-use · keywords: index, sharded query targeting
- [passage] Each index suggestion includes an Average Query Targeting score indicating how many documents were read for every document returned for the index's corresponding query shapes. A score of 1 represents very efficient query shapes because every document read matched the query and was returned with the query results. All suggested indexes represent an opportunity to improve query performance. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor.md#query-targeting · keywords: index, query optimization, query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/
- [passage] When you use `$sort` on a sharded cluster, each shard sorts its result documents using an index where available. Then the [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) or one of the shards performs a streamed merge sort. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sort.md#sort-index-use · keywords: index, sharded query targeting, $sort, mongos
- [passage] - Create the indexes that the Performance Advisor suggests when they align with your [Indexing Strategies.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/applications/indexes/) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/analyze-slow-queries.md#best-practices-for-query-performance · keywords: index, query optimization
- [passage] As with any hash function, two different plan cache query shapes may result in the same hash value. However, the occurrence of hash collisions between different plan cache query shapes is unlikely. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: index, query shape
- [passage] After the [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) receives responses from all shards, it merges the data and returns the result document. The performance of a broadcast operation depends on the overall load of the cluster, as well as variables like network latency, individual shard load, and number of documents returned per shard. Whenever possible, favor operations that result in [targeted operation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md#std-label-sharding-mongos-targeted) over those that result in a broadcast operation. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md#broadcast-operations · keywords: sharded query targeting, mongos · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router/
- [fact] mongos performs a targeted operation when the query includes the shard key or a prefix of a compound shard key. For key {a:1,b:1,c:1} the usable prefixes are {a:1} and {a:1,b:1}. A query on {b:1} alone is not a prefix and broadcasts. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router/ · keywords: sharded query targeting, Sharded Query Targeting and Scatter-Gather
- [passage] When run without [localOps:true](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentop.md#std-label-currentOp-stage-localOps) on the [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos), the transaction information is per shard. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentOp.md#mongos-composite-view-output · keywords: sharded query targeting, mongos

- [passage] A [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) instance with the [`loadRoutingTableOnStartup`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.loadRoutingTableOnStartup) parameter enabled may experience longer startup times, but will result in faster servicing of initial client connections once started. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#sharding-parameters · keywords: sharded query targeting, mongos, loadRoutingTableOnStartup
- [passage] When a query accesses a shard, a [chunk migration](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/migrate-chunks-in-sharded-cluster.md#std-label-migrate-chunks-sharded-cluster) or [DDL operation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions-operations.md#std-label-transactions-operations-ddl) may already hold the critical section for the collection. If the query finds the critical section is taken, the shard waits until the critical section has been released. When the shard returns control to [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos), [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) retries the query. However, if a multi-shard transaction interacts with an operation that takes the critical section on multiple shards, the interaction can result in a distributed deadlock. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#sharding-parameters · keywords: sharded query targeting, mongos
- [passage] A [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) instance with this parameter enabled may experience longer startup times, but will result in faster servicing of initial client connections once started. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#error-response · keywords: sharded query targeting, mongos

- [passage] The fields in the `mechanisms` document depend on the configuration of the [`authenticationMechanisms`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.authenticationMechanisms) parameter. The `mechanisms` document includes a field for each authentication mechanism supported by your [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) or [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) instance. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md#security · keywords: sharded query targeting, mechanisms, authenticationMechanisms, mongod, mongos
- [passage] - `true` when the [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) / [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) instance's TLS/SSL certificate is associated with a certificate authority. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md#security · keywords: sharded query targeting, true, mongod, mongos
- [passage] When run on a [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos), a document with data about the [transactions](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md#std-label-transactions) run on the instance. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md#mongod · keywords: sharded query targeting, mongos
- [passage] When inserting documents with monotonically increasing shard keys, all inserts belong to the same [chunk](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-chunk) on a single [shard](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-shard). The system eventually divides the chunk range that receives all write operations and migrates its contents to distribute data more evenly. However, at any moment the cluster directs insert operations only to a single shard, which creates an insert throughput bottleneck. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md#shard-key-limitations · keywords: sharded query targeting
- [passage] - [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) includes a [Full Time Diagnostic Data Capture](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/full-time-diagnostic-data-capture.md#std-label-ftdc-stub) mechanism to assist MongoDB engineers with troubleshooting deployments. If this thread fails, it terminates the originating process. To avoid the most common failures, confirm that the user running the process has permissions to create the FTDC `diagnostic.data` directory. For `mongod` the directory is within [`storage.dbPath`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options.md#mongodb-setting-storage.dbPath). For `mongos` it is parallel to [`systemLog.path`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options.md#mongodb-setting-systemLog.path) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#considerations · keywords: sharded query targeting, mongod, diagnostic.data, storage.dbPath, mongos, systemLog.path · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md
- [passage] Specifies a file location to store the process ID (PID) of the `mongod` process. The user running the `mongod` or `mongos` process must be able to write to this path. If the [`--pidfilepath`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#std-option-mongod.--pidfilepath) option is not specified, the process does not create a PID file. Use this option mainly with the [`--fork`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#std-option-mongod.--fork) option. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#core-options · keywords: sharded query targeting, mongod, mongos, --pidfilepath, --fork
- [passage] Allows the `mongod` to accept and create authenticated and non-authenticated connections to and from other `mongod` and [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) instances in the deployment. Used for performing rolling transition of replica sets or sharded clusters from a no-auth configuration to [internal authentication](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/security-internal-authentication.md#std-label-inter-process-auth). Requires specifying a [internal authentication](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/security-internal-authentication.md#std-label-inter-process-auth) mechanism such as [`--keyFile`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#std-option-mongod.--keyFile) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#core-options · keywords: sharded query targeting, mongod, mongos, --keyFile
- [passage] For example, if using [keyfiles](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/security-internal-authentication.md#std-label-internal-auth-keyfile) for [internal authentication](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/security-internal-authentication.md#std-label-inter-process-auth), the `mongod` creates an authenticated connection with any `mongod` or [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) in the deployment using a matching keyfile. If the security mechanisms do not match, the `mongod` uses a non-authenticated connection instead. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#core-options · keywords: sharded query targeting, mongod, mongos
- [passage] The [config database](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-config-database) maintains a map identifying which documents are on which shards. The cluster updates this map as [chunks](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-chunk) move between shards. When a configuration server becomes inaccessible, certain sharding operations become unavailable, such as moving chunks and starting [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) instances. However, clusters remain accessible from already-running [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) instances. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/monitoring.md#config-servers · keywords: sharded query targeting, mongos
- [passage] Because inaccessible configuration servers can seriously impact the availability of a sharded cluster, you should monitor your configuration servers to ensure that the cluster remains well balanced and that [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) instances can restart. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/monitoring.md#config-servers · keywords: sharded query targeting, mongos
- [passage] When run on a [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos), [`$currentOp`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentop.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-currentOp) returns the opids in the format of `"<shardName>:<opid on that shard>"`; e.g. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.killOp.md#kill-write-operations · keywords: sharded query targeting, mongos, $currentOp, "<shardName>:<opid on that shard>"
- [passage] In sharded clusters, MongoDB records query statistics separately on each mongod and mongos when $queryStats is enabled. Shard servers also record statistics for queries that originate from mongos. These provide more complete shard-level metrics for queries that users route through mongos. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: sharded query targeting · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats.md
- [passage] When a user creates a session on a [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) or [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) instance, the record of the session initially exists only in-memory on the instance; i.e. the record is local to the instance. Periodically, the instance will sync its cached sessions to the [`system.sessions`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/config-database.md#mongodb-data-config.system.sessions) collection in the `config` database, at which time, they are visible to [`$listSessions`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/listsessions.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-listSessions) and all members of the deployment. Until the session record exists in the `system.sessions` collection, you can only list the session via the [`$listLocalSessions`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/listlocalsessions.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-listLocalSessions) operation. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/listLocalSessions.md#definition · keywords: sharded query targeting, mongod, mongos, system.sessions, config, $listSessions · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/listSessions.md
- [passage] Hashed indexing is ideal for shard keys with fields that change [monotonically](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharding-choose-a-shard-key.md#std-label-shard-key-monotonic) like [ObjectId](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-ObjectId) values or timestamps. When you use [ranged sharding](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/ranged-sharding.md#std-label-sharding-ranged) with a monotonically increasing shard key value, the chunk with an upper bound of [`MaxKey`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mongodb-extended-json.md#mongodb-bsontype-MaxKey) receives the majority incoming writes. This behavior restricts insert operations to a single shard, which removes the advantage of distributed writes in a sharded cluster. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-hashed.md#use-cases · keywords: sharded query targeting, MaxKey · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-hashed/create.md
- [passage] mongos performs a broadcast operation for queries that do not include the shard key, routing queries to all shards in the cluster. Some queries that do include the shard key may still result in a broadcast operation depending on the distribution of data in the cluster and the selectivity of the query. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router/ · keywords: sharded query targeting · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md
- [passage] With RBAC enforced, clients must specify a --username, --password, and --authenticationDatabase when connecting to the mongos in order to access cluster resources. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router/ · keywords: sharded query targeting
- [passage] - MongoDB Compass shows limited performance data when connected to a [`mongos`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/compass/performance.md#limitations · keywords: sharded query targeting, mongos

## How-to and procedures

- [passage] To improve query performance for [time series collections](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-time-series-collection), add one or more [secondary indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-secondary-index) to support common time series query patterns. Starting in MongoDB 6.3, MongoDB automatically creates a [compound index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound.md#std-label-index-type-compound) on the `metaField` and `timeField` fields for new collections. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-secondary-index.md · keywords: index, query optimization, query shape, metaField, timeField
- [passage] To improve query performance, [create one or more secondary indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-secondary-index.md#std-label-timeseries-add-secondary-index) on your `timeField` and `metaField` to support common query patterns. In versions 6.3 and higher, MongoDB creates a secondary index on the `timeField` and `metaField` automatically. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-best-practices.md#create-secondary-indexes · keywords: index, query optimization, query shape, timeField, metaField · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-best-practices/
- [passage] To analyze query performance, see [Interpret Explain Plan Results.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan.md) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md#create-indexes-to-support-queries · keywords: index, query optimization
- [passage] To view the MongoDB 8.0 `queryShapeHash` and `planCacheShapeHash` hexadecimal strings, you can use the [`explain`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/explain.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.explain) command. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md#matching-query-shapes · keywords: index, query shape, queryShapeHash, planCacheShapeHash, explain
- [passage] To enable log redaction on a running `mongod` or `mongos`, use the following command: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#logging-parameters · keywords: sharded query targeting, mongod, mongos

- [passage] To detect if the MongoDB instance that your client is connected to is mongos, use the hello command. - [passage] Use Self-Managed Internal/Membership Authentication to enforce intra-cluster security and prevent unauthorized cluster components from accessing the cluster. You must start each mongod or mongos in the cluster with the appropriate security settings in order to enforce internal authentication. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router/ · keywords: sharded query targeting · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md
- [passage] Avoid overloading the connection resources of a [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) or [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) instance by adjusting the connection pool size to suit your use case. Start at 110-115% of the typical number of current database requests, and modify the connection pool size as needed. Refer to the [Connection Pool Options](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/connection-string-options.md#std-label-connection-pool-options) for adjusting the connection pool size. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/production-notes.md#manage-connection-pool-sizes · keywords: sharded query targeting, mongod, mongos
- [passage] To achieve an even data distribution across all shards in the cluster, a balancer runs in the background to migrate ranges across the shards. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/sharding/ · keywords: sharded query targeting
- [passage] to a shard. Please connect to the cluster via a router (mongos)." — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/sharding/ · keywords: sharded query targeting
- [passage] To run a non-supported database command directly against a node in a sharded cluster, you must either connect to mongos or have the maintenance-only directShardOperations role. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/sharding/ · keywords: sharded query targeting

## Measurements and reference values

- [fact] Queries that involve multiple shards per request are less efficient and do not scale linearly when shards are added. A Netdata guide estimates a scatter-gather query on a 50-shard cluster can use up to 50x the CPU, memory and I/O of a targeted query. The 50x figure is an unbenchmarked estimate, not a measured number. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharding-choose-a-shard-key/ · keywords: sharded query targeting, Sharded Query Targeting and Scatter-Gather

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. This flag is required when the output of an endpoint is binary (ex: gzip) and the command is not piped (ex: atlas command > out.zip) | | --pretty | | false | Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format. | | --processIds | processId | false | Process IDs from which to retrieve query shape statistics. A processId is a combination of host and port that serves the MongoDB process. The host must be the hostname, FQDN, IPv4 address, or IPv6 address of the host that runs the MongoDB process (`mongod` or `mongos`). The port must be the IANA port on which the MongoDB process listens for requests. To include multiple `processIds`, pass the parameter multiple times delimited with an ampersand (`&`) between each `processId`. | | --queryShapeHash | $queryStats | true | A SHA256 hash of a query shape, output by MongoDB commands like $queryStats and `$explain` or slow query logs. | | --since | int | false | Date and time from which to retrieve query shape statistics. This parameter expresses its value in the number of milliseconds that have elapsed since the [UNIX epoch]([https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time)). If you don't specify the **until** parameter, the endpoint returns data covering from the **since** value and the current time.; If you specify neither the **since** nor the **until** parameters, the endpoint returns data from the previous 24 hours. | | --until | int | false | Date and time up until which to retrieve query shape statistics. - [passage] Wildcard indexes store entries for the contents of a document or array, not the document or array itself. Therefore, wildcard indexes cannot support exact equality matches on documents or arrays. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/restrictions.md#equality-matches-on-documents-and-arrays · keywords: index, query shape
- [passage] For example, consider an `inventory` collection with a wildcard index on `product_attributes`. - [passage] | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `profile` | int | Configures the profiler level. The following profiler levels are available: `0`The profiler is off and does not collect any data. This is the default profiler level.`1`The profiler collects data for operations that exceed the `slowms` threshold or match a specified [filter.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.setprofilinglevel.md#std-label-set-profiling-level-options-filter)When a filter is set:The `slowms` and `sampleRate` options are not used for profiling.; The profiler only captures operations that match the [filter.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.setprofilinglevel.md#std-label-set-profiling-level-options-filter)`2`The profiler collects data for all operations.When set to level `2`, the profiler ignores user provided values for `slowms` and `filter`. Since profiling is not available on [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos), the [`profile`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/profile.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.profile) command cannot be used to set the profiling level to a value other than `0` on a [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) instance. | | `slowms` | int | Optional. Default: 100 The slow operation time threshold, in milliseconds. Operations that run for longer than this threshold are considered *slow*. Slow operations are logged based on `workingMillis`, which is the amount of time that MongoDB spends working on that operation. This means that factors such as waiting for locks and flow control do not affect whether an operation exceeds the slow operation threshold. When [`logLevel`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.logLevel) is set to `0`, MongoDB records *slow* operations to the diagnostic log at a rate determined by [`slowOpSampleRate`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options.md#mongodb-setting-operationProfiling.slowOpSampleRate) At higher `logLevel` settings, all operations appear in the diagnostic log regardless of their latency with the following exception: the logging of slow oplog entry messages by the secondaries. The secondaries log only the slow oplog entries; increasing the `logLevel` does not log all oplog entries. This argument affects the same setting as the configuration option [`operationProfiling.slowOpThresholdMs`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options.md#mongodb-setting-operationProfiling.slowOpThresholdMs) | | `sampleRate` | double | Optional. Default: 1.0 The fraction of *slow* operations that should be profiled or logged. `sampleRate` accepts values between 0 and 1, inclusive. This argument affects the same setting as the configuration option [`operationProfiling.slowOpSampleRate`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options.md#mongodb-setting-operationProfiling.slowOpSampleRate) and does not affect the slow oplog entry log messages on secondaries. | | `filter` | object | Optional. A query that determines which operations are profiled or logged. The filter query takes the following form: `{ <field1>: <expression1>, ... }` The query can be any legal [`find()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.find) operation where the query `<field>` matches a field in the [profiler output.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#std-label-profiler) This argument affects the same setting as the configuration option [`operationProfiling.filter`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options.md#mongodb-setting-operationProfiling.filter). When `filter` is set, the `slowms` and `sampleRate` options are not used for profiling and slow-query log lines. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/profile.md#command-fields · keywords: sharded query targeting, profile, The profiler collects data for operations that exceed the , slowms, sampleRate, , the profiler ignores user provided values for  · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.setProfilingLevel.md

- [passage] The `tcpFastOpenQueueSize` parameter sets the size of the queue of pending TFO connections. - [passage] All updateOne(), replaceOne() and deleteOne() operations must include the shard key or _id in the query document. MongoDB returns an error if these methods are used without the shard key or _id. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router/ · keywords: sharded query targeting
- [passage] The mongos binary cannot connect to mongod instances whose feature compatibility version (FCV) is greater than that of the mongos. For example, you cannot connect a MongoDB 4.0 version mongos to a 4.2 sharded cluster with FCV set to 4.2. You can, however, connect a MongoDB 4.0 version mongos to a 4.2 sharded cluster with FCV set to 4.0. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router/ · keywords: sharded query targeting
- [passage] The [profiler entries](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-the-database-profiler.md#std-label-database-profiler) and the [diagnostic log messages (i.e. mongod/mongos logmessages)](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#std-label-log-message-slow-ops) for read/write operations include: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#logging-slow-operations · keywords: sharded query targeting
- [passage] When you run the sh.shardCollection() method, the balancer begins distributing the collection data to other shards in the cluster. A single shard can only participate in one chunk migration at a time. When MongoDB succeeds in copying a range of data from one shard to another, the range on the donor shard is marked for removal by the range deleter. This process is slow and resource intensive. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/sharding/ · keywords: sharded query targeting

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [passage] Number of times a collection scan occurred during query execution. During a collection scan, each document in a collection is compared to the query predicate. Collection scans occur if no appropriate [index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/indexes.md#std-label-indexes) exists that [covers](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md#std-label-indexes-covered-queries) the query. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#execution-plan-statistics-for-query-with-lookup-pipeline-stage · keywords: index, query optimization, query shape
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 9.0, you can use the `queryKnobs` setting to override internal server parameters for a single [query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md#std-label-query-shapes) instead of the whole instance. Set the `queryKnobs` field for targeted queries to mitigate the impact of one regressed shape without changing behavior for other workloads on the same deployment. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md#query-knobs · keywords: query shape, sharded query targeting, queryKnobs
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 8.0, use query settings instead of adding [index filters](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-index-filters). Index filters are deprecated starting in MongoDB 8.0. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheSetFilter.md#set-filter-on-plan-cache-query-shape-consisting-of-predicate-and-collation · keywords: index, query shape
- [fact] updateOne(), replaceOne() and deleteOne() must include the shard key or _id; otherwise MongoDB returns an error instead of broadcasting. updateMany() and deleteMany() are broadcast unless the query specifies the full shard key. Multi-update operations are always broadcast. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router/ · keywords: sharded query targeting, Sharded Query Targeting and Scatter-Gather
- [passage] Running `$currentOp` with [localOps:true](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentop.md#std-label-currentOp-stage-localOps) provides a composite view of the in-progress transactions run on that [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos), rather than information on individual shards. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentOp.md#mongos-composite-view-output · keywords: sharded query targeting, $currentOp, mongos
- [passage] [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) and [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) do not rely on `disableSplitHorizonIPCheck` for validation at startup. Legacy `mongod` and `mongos` instances that use IP addresses instead of host names can start after an upgrade. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#replication-and-consistency · keywords: sharded query targeting, mongod, mongos, disableSplitHorizonIPCheck

- [passage] Instead, MongoDB uses the wildcard index to support only one of the query predicates. MongoDB automatically chooses which predicate to support based on relevant wildcard index paths. - [passage] This is also true for compound wildcard indexes. - [passage] For queries that don't include the shard key, [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) must query all shards, wait for their responses and then return the result to the application. These "scatter/gather" queries can be long running operations. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md#targeted-operations-vs-broadcast-operations · keywords: sharded query targeting, mongos · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router/
- [passage] [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) instances broadcast queries to all shards for the collection **unless** the [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) can determine which shard or subset of shards stores this data. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md#broadcast-operations · keywords: sharded query targeting, mongos
- [passage] The [`updateMany()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.updatemany.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.updateMany) and [`deleteMany()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.deletemany.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.deleteMany) methods are broadcast operations, unless the query document specifies the shard key in full. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md#broadcast-operations · keywords: sharded query targeting, updateMany(), deleteMany()
- [passage] The [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) program *can* route queries that include the full shard key or either of the following shard key prefixes at a specific shard or set of shards: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md#targeted-operations · keywords: sharded query targeting, mongos · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router/
- [passage] All [`insertOne()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.insertone.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.insertOne) operations target to one shard. Each document in the [`insertMany()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.insertmany.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.insertMany) array targets to a single shard, but there is no guarantee all documents in the array insert into a single shard. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md#targeted-operations · keywords: sharded query targeting, insertOne(), insertMany() · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router/
- [passage] Depending on the distribution of data in the cluster and the selectivity of the query, [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) may still perform a [broadcast operation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md#std-label-sharding-mongos-broadcast) to fulfill these queries. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md#targeted-operations · keywords: sharded query targeting, mongos
- [fact] A query without the shard key is broadcast to all shards for the collection. mongos must query every shard, wait for all responses, then merge. MongoDB calls these scatter/gather queries and says they can be long running. Docs say to favor targeted operations over broadcast ones. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router/ · keywords: sharded query targeting, Sharded Query Targeting and Scatter-Gather
- [fact] Including the shard key does not guarantee a single-shard route. Depending on data distribution and query selectivity, mongos may still broadcast (for example a range predicate spanning chunks on several shards). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router/ · keywords: sharded query targeting, Sharded Query Targeting and Scatter-Gather
- [passage] Zone sharding does not support time series collections. The balancer always distributes data in sharded time series collections evenly across all shards in the cluster. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-considerations.md#zone-sharding · keywords: sharded query targeting · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries-collections.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries-collections/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-limitations.md
- [passage] The IP address (or hostname) and the ephemeral port of the [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) where the operation originates. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentOp.md#output-fields · keywords: sharded query targeting, mongos
- [passage] Commit coordination is handled by a shard, and `$currentOp` (run either on a [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) or a shard member) returns a shard's coordination information only for transactions the shard is currently coordinating. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentOp.md#output-fields · keywords: sharded query targeting, $currentOp, mongos · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/currentOp.md

- [passage] MongoDB mongos instances route queries and write operations to shards in a sharded cluster. mongos provides the only interface to a sharded cluster from the perspective of applications. - [passage] The mongos tracks what data is on which shard by caching the metadata from the config servers. - [passage] Generally, the fastest queries in a sharded environment are those that mongos route to a single shard, using the shard key and the cluster meta data from the config server. - [passage] mongos can route queries that include the shard key or the prefix of a compound shard key a specific shard or set of shards. mongos uses the shard key value to locate the chunk whose range includes the shard key value and directs the query at the shard containing that chunk. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router/ · keywords: sharded query targeting · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/sharding/
